name: Sovereign debt stress
summary: France–Bund 10-year spread widened to 156bp on 17 Nov, above the 150bp Alert line in most sessions since late Oct
state: The France–Germany 10-year spread closed at 156.3bp on 17 Nov, with French yields at 4.91%, up from 142.4bp on 10 Nov, and has closed above 150bp in most sessions since late Oct (Ideal Investisseur). French 10-year yields eased to about 4.85% on 18 Nov after a sell-off driven by ECB rate-rise bets (Trading Economics). The US 10-year yield was about 5.07% on 18 Nov (Yahoo Finance). No failed G7 auction or emergency central-bank buying was found.
for_you: Higher French and US government borrowing costs tend to feed through to mortgage and business loan rates and can tighten public budgets.

why: When big governments struggle to borrow, it raises everyone's costs and can force sudden austerity or money-printing.
drivers: Deficits, auction demand, ratings actions, political shocks, long-end yields.

rubric.alert: Failed G7 auction, emergency central-bank purchases, France–Bund > 150bp, or Italy–Bund > 250bp.
rubric.watch: G7 30-year yields at multi-decade highs, a G7 downgrade, or France–Bund 80–150bp / Italy–Bund 150–250bp.
rubric.normal: Auctions orderly; France–Bund spread < 80bp; Italy–Bund < 150bp; no G7 downgrades this month.
